style: Retro gospel-funk and barrelhouse vocal group fusion, 1960s mono room capture with tape saturation. Harmony: barbershop voice leading with whole-tone chromatic interruptions and delayed gospel cadences. Melody: fast scat-like contours, yodel register flips, and clipped consonant attacks. Rhythm: deep funk pocket with syncopated sixteenth-note displacement and sudden metric compressions. Timbre: fuzz guitar, gospel piano, tambourine, upright bass, and organ swells. Vocal: stacked doo-wop vocables, massed gospel choir, and deadpan spoken narration. Performance: theatrical overstatement delivered with absolute deadpan seriousness. Production: warm analog room bleed with spring reverb. Operators: hold vocal stack fixed while piano migrates; compress the rhythmic downbeat while stretching harmonic resolution; make barbershop chords behave like a heavy funk groove without abandoning vocal identity; preserve the tambourine pulse while destabilizing all harmonic navigation; force incompatible temporal scales to coexist.
lyrics: [Intro] [Slight tape wow and flutter] [Upright bass establishes a heavy, sluggish funk vamp] [Spoken deadpan] Attention. The classification of the color blue as a domestic appliance is now fully operational. [Staccato handclaps] [Verse 1] [Stacked doo-wop vocals singing nonsense vocables] Bom-bom, we put the refrigerator in the toaster! Bom-bom, the refrigerator sings in B-flat! [Gospel piano joins with bright, percussive chords] The kitchen cabinet is a legal corporation! It holds three shares of maritime insurance! [Yodel register flip] Yodelo-hee, the toaster is a soprano in distress! [Chorus] [Massed gospel choir enters with ecstatic harmonic friction] Oh, the silly weird colorful goofy bitch walks through the wall! She is made of absolute fiscal year and three dead batteries! [Call-and-response] Who owns the shadow? (The furniture owns it!) Who owns the math? (The carpet owns it!) [Verse 2] [Fuzz guitar interjects with abrasive, melodic blues lines] Let us measure the humidity of an abstract noun. It weighs four kilograms of Tuesday afternoon. [Patter singing at near-spoken speed] The ceiling fan is calculating long division while spinning backwards into ancient history! [Hocketed vocal fragments passed rapidly between tenors] Tic-toc, the clock is a bucket of wet cement! Tic-toc, the cement is a trombone solo! [Bridge] [Tempo doubles abruptly, driving sixteenth-note rhythm] [A cappella vocal stack with heavy nasal resonance and rolled consonants] Rrrrrr-colossal, mmm-structural, bzzzz-bureaucratic! The category error is eating the dining room table! [Barbershop chord held with ringing dominant tension, then violently unresolved] [Instrumental Interbreak] [Organ swells and tambourine acceleration] [The band plays with manic, physical commitment while the piano drifts into whole-tone clusters] [Verse 3] [Spoken narration over walking bass] We have removed the concept of linear time entirely. In its place we have installed a very polite toaster that insists on shaking hands. [Gospel choir sings sustained open vowels] Ahhhhhhh... [Interrupted by harsh consonant percussive attacks] T-t-t-toaster time! B-b-b-bread space! [Chorus] [Full ensemble returns with maximum kinetic energy] Oh, the silly weird colorful goofy bitch walks through the wall! She is made of absolute fiscal year and three dead batteries! [Call-and-response] Who owns the shadow? (The furniture owns it!) Who owns the math? (The carpet owns it!) [Outro] [Sudden drop to dry, close-miked mono room] [Single deadpan voice speaks directly into the microphone] The classification is complete. The toaster has been successfully elected mayor of the kitchen sink. [Final barbershop chord rings out, perfectly tuned, then abruptly cut off by tape stop] [End]
caption: A frantic gospel-funk collision where household objects are literally classified as legal corporations and appliances. Built on barbershop voice leading, deep funk grooves, and stacked vocal harmonies, the track treats categorical absurdity with deadpan administrative seriousness.
